message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph on rural interstates).
• In cities: 25–35 mph in residential areas, 35–45 mph on main streets.
• “No Speed Limit” zones exist on some rural roads. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• Texas has a “no‑seat‑belt” law for drivers over 18 if the vehicle is a “non‑commercial” vehicle. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | | **Alcohol & Driving** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is DUI.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC 0.02 % or higher). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Buses** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal, check mirrors, and ensure safe distance.
• No passing on the right unless the left lane is occupied. | | **Parking** | • No parking on sidewalks, in front of driveways, or in fire lanes.
• Parking on a curb is prohibited if it blocks traffic. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles must be towed if they pose a hazard.
• The towing company must notify the owner. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Registration must be renewed annually.
• Proof of insurance is required; uninsured drivers face fines and license suspension. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green = go; yellow = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop. | | **Driving Under the Influence (DUI)** | • Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol education, and possible jail time. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles: helmet required for riders under 18; helmets for all riders over 18 if riding a motorcycle with a sidecar.
• Commercial vehicles: stricter regulations on hours of service. | ### How to Find Specific Statutes - **Texas Transportation Code**: The primary source for traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)**: Offers driver’s handbook, updates, and enforcement guidelines. - **Texas Legislature Online**: Search for specific statutes or amendments. ### Quick Resources - **Texas DPS Driver Handbook** – PDF available on the DPS website. - **Texas.gov** – Official state portal with links to traffic regulations. - **Texas A&M Transportation Institute** – Research and policy updates. Feel free to ask if you need details on a particular rule or how to handle a specific situation!
